title: Batch / Cache / Quantization Playbook — Draft Recommendations
content:
Summary:

This is a working draft playbook with concrete recommended settings for batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization targeted at reducing per-token inference cost while respecting 99th-pct latency SLOs. The goal: a repeatable set of knobs teams can apply per-route to get ~20–50% cost reduction depending on workload characteristics.

Scope and assumptions:
- Models: family buckets (small: up to 7B, med: 13–34B, large: 70B+).
- Hardware: A100-80GB, H100, and mixed T4/RTX inference fleet for cheap burst.
- Typical request shapes: chat (avg 120 tokens request, 40 tokens response), completion (avg 40 request, 150 response), embeddings (single short input).
- Latency SLO targets: interactive routes <= 200ms p50, <= 800ms p99; batch-able non-interactive routes p99 <= 3s.
- Cost model: use hosted cost spreadsheet 'optimize/cost-models/2025-q1-costing.xlsx' (tab names referenced below).

High-level recommendations (quick):
1) Batching: enable continuous microbatching for med+large models with adaptive windowing. Target effective batch sizes of 8–32 depending on sequence length and latency headroom.
2) KV/prefix caching: enable prefix KV caching for chat routes with repeatable system and user prompts; TTL 30m for session-scoped cache, evict LRU for memory pressure.
3) Quantization: prefer fp16 for large; int8 for med when accuracy loss <1% on our eval sets; int4 for small/experiments with systematic QA gate.

Detailed settings by route type:

A) Interactive chat routes (low p99 latency budget)
- Batch strategy: continuous batching with max_batch_size=8, max_batch_latency_ms=12. Adaptive increase to 16 when p99 headroom >200ms and hardware util <65%.
- KV/cache: enable user-session prefix cache. Cache keys: hashed (system_prompt + conversation_prefix_last_n=8). TTL default 30 minutes; sticky pin for active sessions (last-access bump). Approx memory: 1.6GB per 1k active sessions (estimate from spreadsheet).
- Quantization: keep fp16 for med/large models used for chat. For <7B, allow int8 quant if eval delta <0.5% BLEU/QA metric.
- Expected savings: batching + cache ~18–28% cost drop for chat; combined with int8 on small models -> up to 35%.

B) Document generation / long completion routes (higher latency allowed)
- Batch strategy: max_batch_size=32, max_batch_latency_ms=1200 (allow multi-second windows for cost efficiency). Use request-priority labeling to not block interactive traffic.
- KV/cache: enable prefix caching only for repeated templates; consider embedding-based similarity dedupe (if request matches cached output >95% similarity) to short-circuit generation.
- Quantization: aggressively use int8 for med models; consider int4 quant for <13B with rigorous eval.
- Expected savings: batching dominant -> 30–50% cost reduction.

C) Embeddings / bulk inference (throughput-first)
- Batch strategy: large static batches (64–512) tuned by GPU memory. Use dedicated capacity pools.
- KV/cache: per-item caching by sha256(input) with long TTL (24h) for idempotent embeddings.
- Quantization: int8-int4 ok for many embedding models if downstream similarity preserved; validate on recall/precision slices.
- Expected savings: >50% compared to naively serving single-request embeddings.

Quantization guidance (practical steps):
- Candidate selection: run model diff eval on curated prompt set (per-catalog evals/quant-eval-2025.jsonl). Metrics: semantic-similarity (cosine), token-level accuracy for structured tasks, hallucination rate.
- Thresholds: allow quantized weight variants when delta(metric) < 1% absolute and no category regressed >2%. For chat LLMs, bias/safty checks must pass.
- Fallback policy: runtime should support automatic fallback to fp16 if sample-level confidence drops below route threshold or if hallucination detectors spike.
- Packaging: ship quantized artifacts as separate model entries in model-catalog with metadata: quant-level=int8,int4, baseline-commit, eval-sha.

KV/prefix cache operational rules:
- What to cache: deterministic prefixes (system prompts, instruction templates, static context). Don’t cache dynamic user signals (timestamps, ephemeral tokens).
- Eviction: LRU with size-based caps per model-shard. Soft-eviction for sessions with >1h inactivity.
- Consistency: cache is eventually consistent across replicas; for strong consistency routes (authenticated financial flows) disable cache or use per-customer sticky routing.
- Metrics to expose in Console: cache-hit-rate (route/model), cache-saved-tokens, avg-response-latency-without-cache, cache-memory-usage.

Cost model references (spreadsheet pointers)
- File: optimize/cost-models/2025-q1-costing.xlsx
  - Tab 'latency_profiles' -> cells B2:B20 (p50/p99 baselines)
  - Tab 'quant-sim' -> range D2:F30 (eval deltas by model family)
  - Tab 'batching-sim' -> summary cell K10 (expected token-cost multiplier by batch size)
- Quick lookup: sheet internal links -> CONFLUENCE-OPT-4987 (analysis notes)

Rollout plan (canary-first pattern):
1) Prepare bundle: model-variant artifacts + runtime config (batching params, cache flags, quant flag).
2) Internal dogfood: route 5% traffic from non-critical product route for 48h. Track latency, cost, quality metrics.
3) Canary ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days if thresholds met. Automatic rollback triggers: p99 latency > target + 20%, quality delta > thresholds in quant checks, cache-error-rate >1%.
4) Post-rollout: 7-day stability watch, capture telemetry snapshots, and update the costing spreadsheet with observed deltas.

Monitoring and alerting:
- Dashboards: per-route cost per 1M tokens, batch-size distribution, cache hit rate, quantization µ-quality metrics (BLEU, similarity), and fallback counts.
- Alerts: sudden drop in cache-hit-rate (>20% drop sustained 10m), quant-fallback spikes, p99 latency regressions.

Open questions / TODOs (critical for next iteration):
- Q1: Benchmarks for int4 on 13B family on H100 (need SRE testbed reservation). Owner: Diego.
- Q2: Define similarity threshold for embeddings short-circuiting (Maya to propose baseline).
- Q3: Cost spreadsheet needs per-region cost multipliers for 2025-EU and APAC — finance input required.
- Q4: Small-model hallucination regressions when quantized observed in earlier ad-hoc tests; need stricter QA harness.

Action items (near-term):
- Create 'quant-eval-2025' job in GH actions and run nightly against held-out eval sets. (Jonah)
- Add the following console widgets: cache-hit-rate heatmap, batch-size histogram, quant-fallback counter (Priya + Console eng).
- Update the cost-model spreadsheet with observed canary deltas after first internal dogfood. (Priya / Finance)

Appendix: sample config snippets (pseudo)
- route: /chat/respond
  - batching: {enabled: true, max_batch: 8, max_wait_ms: 12, adapt_when_util_lt: 0.65, adapt_max_batch: 16}
  - cache: {enabled: true, key_expr: hash(system + last8(user_messages)), ttl_s: 1800, pin_active_sessions: true}
  - quant: {allow_variants: [fp16, int8], fallback_to_fp16_on_quality_drop: true}

- route: /embed/text
  - batching: {enabled: true, fixed_batch: 256}
  - cache: {enabled: true, key_expr: sha256(input), ttl_s: 86400}
  - quant: {preferred: int8}

Notes on documentation and comms:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive but still a draft. We'll convert final recommendations into a product guide under Confluence (CONFLUENCE-OPT-4987) and add example notebooks to the optimize repo.
- Keep a changelog (short freeform) inside the costing spreadsheet tab 'changelog'.

If you want a focused subset next: I can produce a one-page 'canary checklist' (for SRE) or a param sweep notebook (to simulate batch-size tradeoffs using our latency model). Reply with preference.

-- Priya
